thread:
Sam: Quick follow-up to the RFC we posted — I want to propose a small "surface harmonizer" shim that runs at the frontend ingress to translate older client payloads to the new runtime surface. Goal: minimal runtime churn, opt-in via tenant flag. TL;DR: edge shim vs runtime plugin tradeoffs.
Priya: +1 on opt-in. Do we have perf numbers? worried about added p99 latency at the Gateway.
Miguel: We measured a simple field-mapper shim in staging — added ~1.2ms median and ~6-8ms p99 under bursty load (small instances). If we run it in C++ at the gateway path probably similar. Key question: complexity vs ownership.
Jules: Ownership matters. If gateway team owns shim, infra overhead + deploy cadence mismatch. If runtime plugin owns it, we avoid cross-team ops but runtime gets more code paths to maintain.
Sam: Right. Proposal: implement shim as a lightweight Lua filter next to the ingress (low-risk), release as tenant opt-in, and simultaneously build a runtime plugin fallback (longer term). If adoption grows, migrate to runtime.
Priya: Lua is okay but watch out for JSON parsing cost. Could we do header-based short-circuit for the common case? e.g., header X-Compat: v1->v2 so only pay cost when needed.
Miguel: header gating is good. Also record telemetry: shim_invoked, shim_duration_ms, shim_error. Need to make sure logs correlate with tenant_id.
Jules: Also need canary plan: start with 5 internal tenants, then 25, then broad. Rollback button if shim_error_count spikes. infra-bot can create alert.
infra-bot: Created alert rule "shim_error_rate" -> page if >1.5% over 5m for >3 tenants. Dashboard panel added: "Surface Harmonizer - invocations / latency".
Sam: Thanks. Open questions: migration of preserved fields (we can't invent missing fields) and how to handle ambiguous mappings (e.g., freeform user input -> structured instructions).
Priya: For ambiguous mappings, default to pass-through plus a warning header so clients can detect and opt-in to stricter mapping in the future. Document edge cases in the RFC follow-up.
Miguel: I'll sketch the shim pseudocode for review:

```
if header X-Compat == "v1->v2":
  try transform_payload(payload)
  if success:
    set header X-Shim-Applied: true
  else:
    set header X-Shim-Error: reason
    return 400 (if tenant strict) OR forward original with warning (default)
```

Sam: Nice. Let's add metrics and a txn-id in logs for tracing. Also include an opt-out TTL so tenants can revert to runtime mapping if they prefer.
Jules: I'll draft the rollout playbook with cohort list and rollback steps. Also add a note about RBAC for who can flip the opt-in flag.
Priya: One more: security review for any transformation code (avoid executing templates, no eval). Keep transformations deterministic and sandboxed.
Sam: Agreed. Action items: Miguel draft shim code + perf test (ETA 48h), Jules draft rollout playbook (ETA 24h), Priya list security checklist (ETA 48h). We'll reconvene after artifacts. :thumbsup:
